        "Read all nine paths in the complete319-line fetch proposal and317-line inverse, including five native/IDL paths and the full74-line Rust wrapper addition/deletion.         "The proposal moves the checked i32::MAX size limit and native string-stream creation into the safe wrapper. The byte vector is first converted to a real nsCString, then SetByteStringData copies it. The copy reason concerns keeping stream bytes valid beyond the temporary Rust data. A type name or SAFETY comment is not a general lifetime, allocation-free or end-to-end memory-safety proof. The accepted current wrapper preserves the checked limit/copy while using ProtocolError::Size and renamed Exchange interface.",
        "The IDL removes the separate count argument. Offline storage changes from SyncCopyStreamN(count), which errors on early EOF, to SyncCopyStream, which reads to EOF and reports actual bytes written. Both selected native consumers account the returned bytes. The channel already used full-stream copying before this proposal; its now-unused count parameter is removed. No streaming chunk protocol, exact advertised-size guarantee or support for larger-than-i32::MAX payloads is inferred.",
        "The old client ignores OnFetchStart failure and proceeds to GetItem. The proposal invokes checked on_fetch_start inside the fallible inner operation, so a start error stops request construction and reaches failure/stop dispatch. On success the proposal discards the completion callback result. Current shared DoOperation separately warns for callback error, as the already-read common handler shows. Current GetMessage checks exactly one item before unwrap, requires MIME content, decodes base64 and invokes the stream adapter.",
        "Historical/native stop paths preserve cleanup and completion on earlier failures. Offline fetch discards a started output stream on failure, finalizes database linkage on success and invokes doneFn. Channel stop passes failure to OnStopRequest or starts reading the stored message on success; no new all-consumer callback/cancellation guarantee is invented.
